chunks: And it is narrated from Ṣabbāḥ al-Muzanī, raising it, that he said:

Two men came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. One of them said, "O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, this man and I had a meal together. I brought three loaves of bread, and he brought five loaves of bread. Then we ate lunch, and a man passed by us, so we invited him to the meal. He came and ate with us. When we finished, he gifted us eight dirhams and departed. So I said, 'O this man, divide with me.' He said, 'I will only do so according to the measure of the shares of bread.' He said, 'Go and reconcile between yourselves.' He said, 'O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, he refuses to give me except three dirhams while he takes five dirhams, so decide the judgment for us.'"

He said: then he said to him, "O servant of Allah, do you know that three loaves are nine thirds?" He said, "Yes." He said, "And do you know that five loaves are fifteen thirds?" He said, "Yes." He said, "So you ate eight of the nine thirds, and one remained for you. And this man ate eight of the fifteen, and seven remained for him. And the guest ate seven thirds from this man's bread and from your bread this one third that remained from your bread. Thus, each one of you was apportioned eight thirds. So for this man are seven dirhams, in exchange for each third one dirham, and for you, for your one third, is one dirham."
"So take one dirham, and give this man seven dirhams."

key_terms.أَثْلَاثٍ: thirds, the units used in the Imam’s calculation
key_terms.أَرْغِفَةٍ: loaves of bread contributed by the two men
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.الضَّيْفُ: the guest whose consumption determines the fair division
key_terms.الْحِصَصِ: the proportional shares used to determine division
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: judgment or formal adjudication in the dispute
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams given as payment or gift after the meal

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام judge the dispute of the three and five loaves and the eight dirhams?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a dispute brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding how to divide payment received after sharing food with a guest. He resolves it through precise reckoning, showing that entitlement is based on what each person actually contributed to the guest, not merely on the total number of loaves initially brought.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3279 - It is narrated from Sabbah Al-Muzani, who raised it (in chain of narration):
Two men came to Commander of the Faithful (as).
One of them said:
"O Commander of the Faithful, this man and I went out together. I brought three loaves of bread, and he brought five loaves of bread. We had lunch together, and a man passed by us, so we invited him to join us for lunch. He came and ate with us.
When we finished, he gifted us eight dirhams and left.
I said to this man: 'Divide the dirhams with me.'
He said: 'I will not do so except based on the proportion of the shares of the bread.'
Commander of the Faithful (as) said: 'Go and reconcile between yourselves.'
The man replied: 'O Commander of the Faithful, he refuses to give me more than three dirhams while he takes five dirhams. Judge between us.'
Commander of the Faithful (as) said to him: 'O servant of Allah (swt), do you know that three loaves of bread equal nine thirds?'
He said: 'Yes.'
Imam (as) continued: 'And do you know that five loaves of bread equal fifteen thirds?'
He said: 'Yes.'
Imam (as) said: 'You ate from your nine-thirds eight-thirds, leaving you one-third.
And this man ate from his fifteen-thirds eight-thirds, leaving him seven-thirds.
The guest ate seven-thirds from this man's bread and one-third from your bread.
Thus, each of you consumed eight-thirds.
This man is entitled to seven dirhams, one dirham for each remaining third of bread he contributed, and you are entitled to one dirham for the one-third you contributed.
So, take one dirham, and give this man seven dirhams.'"
